subject: Circadian rhythm
hook: CIRCADIAN RHYTHM IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Circadian rhythms are not just responses to the environment; they are endogenous, meaning they are built-in biological processes that persist even in the total absence of external cues.
angle_support: The rhythm persists in constant conditions, i.e. constant darkness, with a period of about 24 hours.
J. S. Szymanski showed that animals are capable of maintaining 24-hour activity patterns in the absence of external cues such as light and changes in temperature.
title: Your Internal Clock Beats Without Sunlight
description: Our bodies run on a self‑sustained 24‑hour timer that doesn’t need light to work. Historic experiments proved the rhythm persists in total darkness, showing it’s built‑in, not just a reaction to the environment.
narration: CIRCADIAN RHYTHM IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume our bodies only follow sunrise and sunset, that sleep and hormone spikes are mere reactions to light. In reality, the clock runs on its own timetable, ticking even when all external cues vanish. It keeps a roughly 24‑hour rhythm without any day‑night signal. Even isolated cells in a petri dish keep the beat, showing the clock is wired into our biology. In 1729 French scientist Jean‑Jacques d’Ortous de Mairan placed Mimosa pudica seedlings in a sealed, pitch‑black box. The leaves continued to fold and unfold every 24 hours for weeks, proving an internal oscillator. Later, J.S. Szymanski showed rodents kept in constant darkness still displayed a 24‑hour activity pattern, confirming endogenous timing. He measured the cycle for ten days, finding a free‑running period of 24.2 hours. Your body’s clock keeps time in darkness, independent of sunrise or sunset, a built‑in rhythm that never stops.
